policy.missingEvidenceRule: Missing evidence is unavailable, never numeric zero.
policy.publicationRule: No Career becomes public score-ready from this staging file alone.

industryDiversity.rule: Square the published broad-sector shares and treat all unpublished residual employment as one 'other' bucket. This can only overstate concentration relative to a fully disaggregated residual.

solasNsb2025.authority: SOLAS Skills and Labour Market Research Unit
solasNsb2025.title: National Skills Bulletin 2025

solasForecast2023.authority: SOLAS Skills and Labour Market Research Unit / Cedefop

csoSes2022.title: Structure of Earnings Survey 2022 — Occupation and Education
csoSes2022.note: CSO publishes Professional occupations median hourly earnings of EUR 32.99 and All Occupational Groups EUR 19.60. All Wave A SOC 2010 codes sit in major group 2 Professional Occupations. This is therefore an official but broad Pay proxy, not an exact Career salary.

projection.proxyReason: Cedefop publishes the forecast at the broader ICT professionals group; the bulletin also warns the 2021 ICT baseline is understated.

shortage_signal.explanation: SOLAS 2025 lists software developers/engineers as a national shortage.

vacancy_intensity.proxyReason: 2025 survey explicitly names software developers; 2024 evidence also named software developers/engineers, so persistence is supported. No occupation-level denominator is published.
vacancy_intensity.reason: Conservative fallback: low vacancy intensity (3) + one persistence point (1). The survey confirms repeated difficult-to-fill mentions but cannot support a vacancy-rate band above low without a denominator.

industry_diversity.proxyReason: SOLAS publishes main-sector shares for the broader ict occupational family, not this exact Career. Residual employment is aggregated into one 'other' bucket as a conservative concentration upper bound.

relative_salary.proxyReason: CSO's official 2022 earnings release provides the closest defensible published Pay measure at SOC major-group scope: Professional occupations. This is broader than the canonical Career and therefore Estimated evidence.
relative_salary.reason: All eight Wave A Careers map to SOC 2010 major group 2 (Professional occupations). The same broad proxy is intentionally used consistently; it must not be displayed as an exact Career salary or used to claim Pay differences within Wave A.

entry_accessibility.proxyReason: Official pathway evidence is converted into the frozen CampCareer Entry Accessibility rubric; the source itself does not publish a CampCareer score.

entry_burden.proxyReason: Official pathway/regulation evidence is converted into the frozen CampCareer Entry Burden rubric; higher means lower burden.

projection.proxyReason: Cedefop forecast is broader than Accountants.

industry_diversity.reason: SOLAS publishes 31% Financial activities, 22% Professional activities, 9% Industry and 8% ICT for the broader Business & Financial family, totalling 70%. This is below the Career Data Foundation's roughly 80% usable-coverage gate, so no HHI score is produced.
